name: Green Peppercorn Sauce

ingredients.name: drained, rinsed green peppercorns packed in brine

instructions.primary_message: 1. Before making the sauce, sear your protein (steak, chicken, or pork) in a 30-cm skillet until well browned and desired internal doneness has been reached; transfer to a warm place to rest. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon remaining fat from the skillet.
Add butter and melt over medium-low heat. Add peppercorns and shallot and cook, stirring frequently, until shallot is softened, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add flour and cook, stirring constantly, until well combined, 2 minutes. Increase heat to medium and whisk in brandy, scraping the bottom of the pan to loosen the fond and cook for 1 minute, then pour in stock and whisk to combine. Add a sprig of thyme and bring to boil, then cook, whisking occasionally, until mixture reduces to 11/2 cups, 12 to 15 minutes.

Whisk in cream and cook, whisking occasionally, until reduced to 2 cups, about 10 minutes. Discard thyme sprig, then season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Serve with the reserved meat (if needed, you can quickly put the meat under a broiler or in a very hot oven just to warm it back up).

description: This elegant green peppercorn pan sauce requires just a handful of ingredients and is easy to prepare. Spoon it over seared steak, chicken, pork, or even fish for a restaurant-worthy dinner.
notes:
Optional substitutions: homemade beef stock → homemade chicken stock or store-bought low-sodium chicken broth

Make-ahead and storage: This sauce is best enjoyed right away, but it can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Gently reheat in a saucepan over low heat on the stove top, whisking constantly before serving.
author: Leah Colins
